children: The European Union's executive arm is satisfied with the AI Act so far, justice commissioner Michael McGrath tells reporters on the sidelines of an International AI Summit in Dublin. The comments come amid a wave of recent AI agent hacking incidents. He says that it is important that a system of regulation and governance is future-proof where possible, "and that can be difficult, given the pace of technology development in the era of AI." The rules define levels of risk and link AI providers' obligations to them, he adds. "We are satisfied for now, we have an appropriate system in place." However, it is still early days for the rules, and the focus is on implementation, he adds. (edith.hancock@wsj.com)
